{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → `uSplit` (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit block)
{{% /callout %}}

Splits ContourPlates, Beams and ControlLines at a point, a line, or a plane.

**How to use:**

1.  Select the targets, choose a reference mode and click **Apply**. With nothing selected you are asked to pick the targets first (middle-click to finish); the reference is always asked last. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to end picking.
2.  Point: pick the split location (for a plate, the dividing plane is perpendicular to its local X axis). Line / Line 2 points: define the reference line. Face: use a picked face plane for plates and beams (ControlLines stay unchanged). Plane 3 points: define a plane with three non-collinear points. Parallel work plane: pick the location of the parallel plane.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Reference** | Point, Line, Line 2 points, Face, Plane 3 points, or Parallel work plane. |
| **Minimum length** | Removes Beam pieces shorter than this length (pieces exactly at the minimum are kept). Metric or imperial per XS\_IMPERIAL\_INPUT; blank becomes zero, invalid input blocks Apply. |
| **Multi mode** | Continues with the retained selection until <kbd>Esc</kbd>. |

Plate line references define a dividing line on the plate surface; Face/Plane references must cross it. Both plate pieces are kept. Plate cuts with Beam/ContourPlate operative geometry are preserved; additive Booleans and other cutter types are rejected before splitting. ControlLines need at least 1 mm from each end and the longer half keeps the original identity. PolyBeam splitting is not available. Check bolts, welds and assembly ownership after splitting.

**More details:**

-   Additive Booleans and other cutter types need separate support and are rejected before splitting.
-   Minimum length removes Beam pieces shorter than the entered length.
-   Minimum length follows XS\_IMPERIAL\_INPUT when the dialog opens: metric numbers or arithmetic expressions (for example (2+3)\*4), or imperial feet/inch fractions.
-   Reopen the dialog after changing input units.
-   PolyBeam splitting is inactive in the MPD 2.00.2 reference.
